data.narrative:
Phantom Space is a growth-stage space and aerospace company founded by Jim Cantrell, Michael D'Angelo, and Michal Prywata. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, representing the core competitive set in Space & Aerospace.

Two standard triangulation methods were evaluated against available data. Peer-median analysis was inapplicable: while 14 same-sector peers exist, none of the filtered subsets—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier—yielded three or more comparable datapoints, the minimum threshold for reliable median extraction. Public-comp anchoring, using the sector's P/S median of 24.4x across six tickers, could not be executed absent Phantom Space's disclosed revenue, a standard gap for private companies.

Without applicable triangulation methods producing quantitative output, this analysis cannot support a specific valuation range at this time. The primary constraint is data availability: private company revenue disclosure remains the binding limitation on revenue multiple approaches, while the narrow stage and tier filters eliminate sufficient peer granularity for direct comparable-company medians. Resolution would require either disclosure of Phantom Space's trailing or forward revenue, or identification of additional growth-stage Space & Aerospace peers with published financials. The sector median multiple (24.4x P/S) provides ceiling-level context but cannot be applied as a standalone anchor without revenue-based scaling.
